verses.zh: 示巴女王听见所罗门因耶和华之名所得的名声，就来要用难解的话试问所罗门。
verses.en: When the queen of Sheba heard about Solomon,[NOTE:1] she came to challenge[NOTE:2] him with difficult questions.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text also has, “to the name of the Lord,” which is very awkward due to its unusual syntax. The phrase is omitted in the parallel passage in 2 Chr 9:1. The word “report” is followed by the preposition ל (lamed) in Isa 23:5 and Hos 7:12 and indicates whom the message came to. And otherwise the collocation of לְשֵׁם (leshem, “to the name”) does not follow either a proper noun or the word report elsewhere in scripture. If retained, perhaps it should be translated, “for the reputation of the Lord.”tn Heb “the report about Solomon.”
Or “test.”
Or “riddles.”

verses.zh: 跟随她到耶路撒冷的人甚多，又有骆驼驮着香料、宝石，和许多金子。她来见了所罗门王，就把心里所有的对所罗门都说出来。
verses.en: She arrived in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] with a great display of pomp,[NOTE:2] bringing with her camels carrying spices,[NOTE:3] a very large quantity of gold, and precious gems. She visited Solomon and discussed with him everything that was on her mind.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “with very great strength.” The Hebrew term חַיִל (khayil, “strength”) may refer here to the size of her retinue (cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV) or to the great wealth she brought with her.
Or “balsam oil.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王将她所问的都答上了，没有一句不明白、不能答的。
verses.en: Solomon answered all her questions; there was no question too complex for the king.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Solomon declared to her all her words; there was not a word hidden from the king which he did not declare to her.” If riddles are specifically in view (see v. 1), then one might translate, “Solomon explained to her all her riddles; there was no riddle too complex for the king.”

verses.zh: 示巴女王见所罗门大有智慧，和他所建造的宫室，
verses.en: When the queen of Sheba saw for herself Solomon’s extensive wisdom,[NOTE:1] the palace[NOTE:2] he had built,
notes: Heb “all the wisdom of Solomon.”
Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 席上的珍馐美味，群臣分列而坐，仆人两旁侍立，以及他们的衣服装饰和酒政的衣服装饰，又见他上耶和华殿的台阶（或译：他在耶和华殿里所献的燔祭），就诧异得神不守舍；
verses.en: the food in his banquet hall,[NOTE:1] his servants and attendants,[NOTE:2] their robes, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings which he presented in the Lord’s temple, she was amazed.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the food on his table.”
Heb “the seating of his servants and the standing of his attendants.”
Heb “there was no breath still in her.”

verses.zh: 对王说：「我在本国里所听见论到你的事和你的智慧实在是真的！
verses.en: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your wise sayings and insight[NOTE:1] was true!
notes: Heb “about your words [or perhaps, “deeds”] and your wisdom.”

verses.zh: 我先不信那些话，及至我来亲眼见了才知道人所告诉我的还不到一半。你的智慧和你的福分越过我所听见的风声。
verses.en: I did not believe these things until I came and saw them with my own eyes. Indeed, I didn’t hear even half the story![NOTE:1] Your wisdom and wealth[NOTE:2] surpass what was reported to me.
notes: Heb “the half was not told to me.”
Heb “good.”

verses.zh: 你的臣子、你的仆人常侍立在你面前听你智慧的话是有福的！
verses.en: Your attendants, who stand before you at all times and hear your wise sayings, are truly happy![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “How happy are your men! How happy are these servants of yours, who stand before you continually, who hear your wisdom!”

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的　神是应当称颂的！他喜悦你，使你坐以色列的国位；因为他永远爱以色列，所以立你作王，使你秉公行义。」
verses.en: May the Lord your God be praised because he favored[NOTE:1] you by placing you on the throne of Israel! Because of the Lord’s eternal love for Israel, he made you king so you could make just and right decisions.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “delighted in.”
Heb “to do justice and righteousness.”

verses.zh: 于是，示巴女王将一百二十他连得金子和宝石，与极多的香料，送给所罗门王。她送给王的香料，以后奉来的不再有这样多。
verses.en: She gave the king 120 talents[NOTE:1] of gold, a very large quantity of spices, and precious gems. The quantity of spices the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon has never been matched.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 9,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV, NLT); CEV “five tons”; TEV “4,000 kilogrammes.”
Heb “there has not come like those spices yet for quantity which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.”

verses.zh: （希兰的船只从俄斐运了金子来，又从俄斐运了许多檀香木（或译：乌木；下同）和宝石来。
verses.en: (Hiram’s fleet, which carried gold from Ophir, also brought from Ophir a very large quantity of fine timber and precious gems.

verses.zh: 王用檀香木为耶和华殿和王宫做栏杆，又为歌唱的人做琴瑟。以后再没有这样的檀香木进国来，也没有人看见过，直到如今。）
verses.en: With the timber the king made supports[NOTE:1] for the Lord’s temple and for the royal palace and stringed instruments[NOTE:2] for the musicians. No one has seen so much of this fine timber to this very day.[NOTE:3])
notes: This Hebrew architectural term occurs only here. The meaning is uncertain; some have suggested “banisters” or “parapets”; cf. TEV, NLT “railings.” The parallel passage in 2 Chr 9:11 has a different word, meaning “tracks,” or perhaps “steps.”
Two types of stringed instruments are specifically mentioned, the כִּנּוֹר (kinnor, “zither” [?]), and נֶבֶל (nevel, “harp”).
Heb “there has not come thus, the fine timber, and there has not been seen to this day.”

verses.zh: 示巴女王一切所要所求的，所罗门王都送给她，另外照自己的厚意馈送她。于是女王和她臣仆转回本国去了。
verses.en: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she requested, besides what he had freely offered her.[NOTE:1] Then she left and returned[NOTE:2] to her homeland with her attendants.
notes: Heb “besides what he had given her according to the hand of King Solomon.”
Heb “turned and went.”

verses.zh: 所罗门每年所得的金子共有六百六十六他连得。
verses.en: Solomon received 666 talents[NOTE:1] of gold per year,[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 50,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV); CEV, NLT “twenty-five tons”; TEV “almost 23,000 kilogrammes.”
Heb “the weight of the gold which came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold.”

verses.zh: 另外还有商人和杂族（杂族在历代下九章十四节是阿拉伯）的诸王，与国中的省长所进的金子。
verses.en: besides what he collected from the merchants,[NOTE:1] traders, Arabian kings, and governors of the land.
notes: Heb “from the traveling men.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王用锤出来的金子打成挡牌二百面，每面用金子六百舍客勒；
verses.en: King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold; 600 measures[NOTE:1] of gold were used for each shield.
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “six hundred,” with no unit of measure given.

verses.zh: 又用锤出来的金子打成盾牌三百面，每面用金子三弥那，都放在黎巴嫩林宫里。
verses.en: He also made 300 small shields of hammered gold; three minas[NOTE:1] of gold were used for each of these shields. The king placed them in the Palace of the Lebanon Forest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Three minas. The mina was a unit of measure for weight.

The Palace of the Lebanon Forest. This name was appropriate because of the large amount of cedar, undoubtedly brought from Lebanon, used in its construction. The cedar pillars in the palace must have given it the appearance of a forest.

verses.zh: 王用象牙制造一个宝座，用精金包裹。
verses.en: The king made a large throne decorated with ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.zh: 宝座有六层台阶，座的后背是圆的，两旁有扶手，靠近扶手有两个狮子站立。
verses.en: There were six steps leading up to the throne, and the back of it was rounded on top. The throne had two armrests with a statue of a lion standing on each side.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[There were] armrests on each side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.”

verses.zh: 六层台阶上有十二个狮子站立，每层有两个：左边一个，右边一个；在列国中没有这样做的。
verses.en: There were 12 statues of lions on the six steps, one lion at each end of each step. There was nothing like it in any other kingdom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “nothing like it had been made for all the kingdoms.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王一切的饮器都是金子的。黎巴嫩林宫里的一切器皿都是精金的。所罗门年间，银子算不了甚么。
verses.en: All of King Solomon’s cups were made of gold, and all the household items in the Palace of the Lebanon Forest were made of pure gold. There were no silver items, for silver was not considered very valuable in Solomon’s time.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there was no silver, it was not regarded as anything in the days of Solomon.”

verses.zh: 因为王有他施船只与希兰的船只一同航海，三年一次，装载金银、象牙、猿猴、孔雀回来。
verses.en: Along with Hiram’s fleet, the king had a fleet of large merchant ships[NOTE:1] that sailed the sea. Once every three years the fleet[NOTE:2] came into port with cargoes of[NOTE:3] gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “a fleet of Tarshish [ships].” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.
Heb “the fleet of Tarshish [ships].”
Heb “came carrying.”
The meaning of this word is unclear. Some suggest “baboons.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王的财宝与智慧胜过天下的列王。
verses.en: King Solomon was wealthier and wiser than any of the kings of the earth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth with respect to wealth and with respect to wisdom.”

verses.zh: 普天下的王都求见所罗门，要听　神赐给他智慧的话。
verses.en: Everyone[NOTE:1] in the world wanted to visit Solomon to see him display his God-given wisdom.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta have “all the kings of the earth.” See 2 Chr 9:23.
Heb “and all the earth was seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which God had placed in his heart.”

verses.zh: 他们各带贡物，就是金器、银器、衣服、军械、香料、骡马，每年有一定之例。
verses.en: Year after year visitors brought their gifts, which included items of silver, items of gold, clothes, perfume, spices, horses, and mules.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they were bringing each one his gift, items of silver…and mules, the matter of a year in a year.”

verses.zh: 所罗门聚集战车马兵，有战车一千四百辆，马兵一万二千名，安置在屯车的城邑和耶路撒冷，就是王那里。
verses.en: Solomon accumulated[NOTE:1] chariots and horses. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses. He kept them in assigned cities and in Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “gathered.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.tn Heb “he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.”

verses.zh: 王在耶路撒冷使银子多如石头，香柏木多如高原的桑树。
verses.en: The king made silver as plentiful[NOTE:1] in Jerusalem as stones; cedar was[NOTE:2] as plentiful as sycamore fig trees are in the foothills.[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “as plentiful” are added for clarification.
Heb “he made.”
The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

verses.zh: 所罗门的马是从埃及带来的，是王的商人一群一群按着定价买来的。
verses.en: Solomon acquired his horses from Egypt[NOTE:1] and from Que; the king’s traders purchased them from Que.
notes: From Egypt. Because Que is also mentioned, some prefer to see in vv. 28-29 a reference to Mutsur. Que and Mutsur were located in Cilicia/Cappadocia (in modern southern Turkey). See HALOT 625 s.v. מִצְרַיִם.

verses.zh: 从埃及买来的车，每辆价银六百舍客勒，马每匹一百五十舍客勒。赫人诸王和亚兰诸王所买的车马，也是按这价值经他们手买来的。
verses.en: They paid 600 silver pieces for each chariot from Egypt and 150 silver pieces for each horse. They also sold chariots and horses to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Syria.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and a chariot went up and came out of Egypt for six hundred silver [pieces], and a horse for one hundred fifty, and in the same way to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram by their hand they brought out.”
